note:
v5, THE PLAYER WHO STAYS ON TIME (whole-song draw; rewriting the seven-pair crossing at 1:47–2:17, not the listening-card passages). After the two clocks play on their own, the right guitar becomes the straight clock. It plays the riff’s three low-call accents and four answer notes an octave up, leaving out the muted pedal strokes. It plays precisely the same two bars seven times. The left still borrows time, so its first answer starts six, four, two sixteenths late, then together, then two, four, six early. The right guitar has gone from leader to follower without changing a note.
At about 2:02 the left comes up to the right’s octave and leaves out its muted strokes for just the four-note reply. I checked the written attacks, pitches, gates and velocities: the two parts agree there, not just on the downbeat. The bass stays below. The next time around, the left is lower and its answer gets there first. Both guitars keep their existing rigs and positions; bass, kit, keys, lyre, twelve-string and reverse pickups are unedited.
